style_when: the article is a purely conceptual synthesis or policy dilemma where no physical facility, machine, or supply chain exists, and an elegant abstract paper silhouette states the idea. Never reach for paper collage when the story describes physical manufacturing, freight, energy, hardware, or heavy infrastructure — use cinematic still or telephoto industry instead
prompt: Split-screen diptych paper collage on a worn drafting table at the edge of a data hall: left panel, a massive asymmetric heap of hundreds of hand-torn manila file folders in bone white and graphite, topped by one tarnished cobalt enamel badge; right panel, two neat manila folders holding a small stack of blank paper file cards, with four bright cobalt enamel badges in a tidy row. Rag paper with visible fibre, physical cast shadows falling right, one raking key light from the upper left. Palette: bone white, graphite, cobalt. Split-screen diptych, alternating asymmetry between panels, no legible text, no numerals.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, illegible words, numerals, UI elements
rationale: Paper collage suits a purely conceptual AI memory-store economics without defaulting to a generic datacenter shot. Hand-torn folders and enamel badges make the model-version mismatch legible, and a split-screen diptych directly captures the two-generation contrast.
cue: A memory store belongs to a model version
subject: two paper-craft memory stores—hundreds of manila file folders with one badge versus two slim folders with four badges—on a drafting table in a data hall
core_thesis: A memory store belongs to a model version: the history length at which written state beats re-reading is set by the reader, so a folder and a write rule tuned on one model are mispriced after an upgrade.
core_conflict: Write-path overproduction versus reader capacity: one model over-writes hundreds of files for one badge while a later model curates a few files for four badges, and the crossover depends on the reader’s hold on the log.
composition: split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast
